evaluated.name: WeakestLinkCashDiscipline
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), sale))), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ni, sale), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Credible cash-backed performance requires passing two tests at once — working capital that is not swelling relative to sales, and a net margin that is stable across years — so a firm is only as trustworthy as its weaker dimension.
evaluated.reasoning: The minimum of two goodness ranks equals one minus the maximum of the two badness ranks, a genuinely non-additive conjunction whose top decile can only be reached by firms that are jointly low-accrual and stable-margin, fixing the earlier product-of-badness structure whose long leg pooled mixed cases. Scaling working-capital accruals by sales rather than assets ties the accrual to the revenue base that generates it, and margin volatility is the quality dimension least contaminated by leverage or negative book equity.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SoftAccrualStabilityAmplified
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(recch, invch), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Receivable and inventory accruals are the least verifiable ("soft") components of earnings, and their information content is strongest for firms whose gross margins are otherwise stable, because in a stable-margin firm an unexplained soft-accrual build cannot be attributed to genuine operating turbulence.
evaluated.reasoning: The cash-flow-statement items enter with their native sign (cash released when receivables and inventories fall), so a high centered value means collections and inventory discipline, and the gross-margin stability rank acts as a continuous multiplicative weight rather than a hard gate that creates a mass point at zero. Because the accrual term is cross-sectionally centered, the weight steepens the slope on both tails for stable-margin firms and shrinks noisy, turbulent firms toward neutral.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TaxCorroboratedEarningsTrend
evaluated.expression: NEG(SUB(TREND(RATIO(ni, sale), 5), TREND(RATIO(txp, sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A multi-year improvement in reported margins is only credible if it is corroborated by a parallel build in tax obligations; earnings trends unaccompanied by taxes owed reflect book-only accrual recognition that reverses.
evaluated.reasoning: This uses the tax-accrual channel as an external validator of the quality theme's earnings-persistence trend, an interaction with no counterpart in a standard accrual level sort. Firms whose margin trend runs far ahead of their tax-accrual trend are flagged as accounting-driven and should underperform, while firms whose taxes owed keep pace with reported margins have economically real income.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AccrualSmoothingDetector
evaluated.expression: NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(VOL(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), sale), 5), VOL(RATIO(ni, sale), 5)), 1))
evaluated.hypothesis: Smooth reported earnings are a quality signal only when they are not manufactured: if working-capital accruals swing far more than reported margins, accruals are absorbing operating shocks and the apparent stability is an artifact of accounting discretion.
evaluated.reasoning: The ratio directly measures how much work the accrual process does per unit of reported earnings variability, so it separates naturally stable firms (low ratio, high signal) from smoothers whose earnings stability is purchased with volatile accruals. This attacks the theme interaction from the second-moment side rather than the level side, and therefore cannot be a repackaging of any accrual or earnings-volatility level sort.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: InventoryBuildVsDemand
evaluated.expression: NEG(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(NEG(invch), cogs), GROWTH(revt, 1)), 1))
evaluated.hypothesis: Inventory accumulation is only legitimate when it is matched by growing demand; a firm adding inventory equal to a rising fraction of its annual cost of sales while revenue stagnates is accruing future writedowns rather than building durable earnings power.
evaluated.reasoning: This drops apalch (which perversely rewarded payable stretching) and replaces the gross-profit denominator, whose sign flips for weak firms, with cogs — positive for essentially all operating firms — so the accrual is expressed as a change in days-of-inventory. The interaction is a genuine mismatch test between an accruals-exclusive stock build and the quality theme's revenue-growth base, not a rescaled accrual level: identical inventory builds score very differently depending on whether demand is expanding.

evaluated.name: CashBackedMarginTrendProduct
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(TREND(RATIO(ni, sale), 5)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), sale))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A multi-year improvement in net margin earns a return premium only when working capital is not absorbing the improvement; accrual-financed margin gains should be shorted, not treated as neutral, because they reverse as working capital unwinds.
evaluated.reasoning: Multiplying two non-negative goodness ranks makes the top of the distribution reachable only in the doubly-good corner (improving margins and released working capital), while accrual-heavy improvers have a near-zero accrual rank and therefore fall into the short leg rather than to a neutral midpoint — the exact sign defect flagged in the previous version. Against the accepted MIN-based signal it isolates two design choices at once: smooth product versus weakest-link conjunction, and margin trend versus margin volatility as the quality dimension.

evaluated.name: AccrualPurityProfitStreak
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Earnings persistence is better captured by an uninterrupted record of positive margins than by low margin volatility; low non-cash accruals are informative about durable cash earnings specifically for firms that have proven repeatedly that they can earn a profit at all.
evaluated.reasoning: The base is the cash-excluded accrual, centered so both tails are active, and the modifier is a continuous rank of the five-year count of profitable years, which avoids both the VOL channel that inverted in gen 1 and the zero mass point of a hard indicator gate. Paired with Signal 1, this isolates the quality-channel choice (persistence count versus volatility) while holding the repaired accrual primitive constant.

evaluated.name: SoftAccrualDemandMismatchRank
evaluated.expression: SUB(RANK(GROWTH(revt, 1)), RANK(RATIO(NEG(ADD(recch, invch)), cogs)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Revenue expansion is high quality only when it is not absorbed into receivables and inventory; the informative variable is the *gap* between demand growth and soft-accrual build, and it should be measured in rank space because the raw ratio's tails, not its middle, drove the gen-1 result.
evaluated.reasoning: InventoryBuildVsDemand had the strongest FF5 alpha in the archive (t=2.30) but a wrong-signed FMB slope, the classic symptom of a raw-difference construction whose extreme values dominate the decile spread while the middle of the distribution is noisy or non-monotone. Converting both legs to cross-sectional ranks before differencing makes the relation monotone and comparable across firms, and adding receivables to inventory broadens the soft-accrual concept to the full operating cycle.

evaluated.name: MatureFirmCashConversion
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(recch, invch), sale), 1)), RANK(RATIO(re, at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Working-capital accruals carry different information across the corporate life cycle: in a firm with a large stock of accumulated retained earnings, a receivables or inventory build is discretion rather than necessary growth financing, whereas in a young, low-retained-earnings firm the same build is the mechanical cost of expansion.
evaluated.reasoning: Retained earnings over assets is a durability/lifecycle proxy from the quality menu that is a level rather than a second moment, so it sidesteps the volatility channel that inverted, and it enters as a non-negative weight that steepens the accrual slope for seasoned firms and shrinks young firms toward neutral. This tests whether the accruals effect is concentrated in mature, self-financed firms — a conditioning story distinct from profitability persistence.

evaluated.name: ChronicCashConversionMarginTrend
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(ADD(recch, invch), sale), 5)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A single year of cash-favorable working-capital flows is noise; five years of cumulative cash release combined with an improving gross margin identifies firms whose reported improvement is structurally cash-backed rather than accrual-financed.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the accrual *level* with a five-year cumulative flow, a persistence concept, and pairs it conjunctively with a margin *trend* so the long leg requires both chronic cash conversion and genuine profitability improvement. It tests whether the accruals x quality interaction is a slow-moving regime property rather than an annual event, which would also explain the weak annual-level FMB slopes seen so far.

evaluated.name: TaxCorroborationConjunction
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(TREND(RATIO(ni, sale), 5)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(txp, sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Rising reported margins are credible only when tax obligations rise alongside them; requiring both trends to be high simultaneously identifies firms whose book income improvement is corroborated by the tax authorities' claim on it.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-1 difference-of-trends version produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.195) and a positive alpha but also awarded top scores to the economically incoherent case of falling margins with rising taxes payable; the weakest-link conjunction removes that contamination from the long leg while preserving the corroboration mechanism. Because both legs are trends of levels scaled by sales, this also keeps the coverage profile of the gen-1 version rather than trading evidence for a sparser sample.

evaluated.name: CashAccumulationVsBookProfit
evaluated.expression: SUB(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(che, 3), sale)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(re, 3), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Genuinely cash-backed profits eventually show up as a build in the cash balance, so over a multi-year window the accumulation of retained earnings should be tracked by the accumulation of cash; firms whose book profits pile up in retained earnings without any corresponding cash build are reporting accounting profit that never became spendable resources.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the rejected MIN-of-two-published-anomalies structure entirely and replaces both legs: the accruals channel is now the change in the cash stock itself (`che`, an accruals-exclusive primitive never used so far), and the quality channel is the accumulation of retained profits (`re`), so the signal is a stock-level corroboration test rather than a flow-accrual sort combined with earnings smoothness. The three-year differencing horizon smooths one-off financing and dividend timing, and rank differencing keeps the comparison monotone and scale-free, addressing the raw-difference tail sensitivity seen in gen 1.

evaluated.name: AccrualPurityGrossProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-purged low accruals identify durable earnings specifically among firms with genuine operating profitability; for firms whose gross profit per unit of assets is weak, accrual conservatism reflects shrinking operations rather than cash-backed performance.
evaluated.reasoning: This keeps the archive's only doubly-significant accrual primitive fixed and replaces the coarse six-valued profit streak with a continuous gross-profitability rank, directly answering the critic's concern that the conditioner's granularity limited the interaction. Gross profitability is a level, not a second moment, so it avoids the volatility channel that inverted four times in gen 1, and the comparison against the streak version isolates whether the conditioning content is profitability *magnitude* or profitability *reliability*.

evaluated.name: DebtFinancedAccrualBuild
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(dltt, 1), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual quality matters most where the accrual is externally financed: a working-capital build funded by new long-term borrowing commits the firm to fixed claims against earnings that have not yet converted to cash, so accrual reversal turns into genuine financial stress rather than a harmless accounting unwind.
evaluated.reasoning: This introduces the financing side of the balance sheet (`dltt`) as the quality modifier, an economic channel absent from the archive, and it amplifies the accrual slope symmetrically — debt-financed accrual builders sit in the short leg while cash-backed firms that can still access debt markets sit in the long leg. It tests a distinct hypothesis about *why* the interaction exists (financing fragility) rather than *who* has quality earnings (profitability).

evaluated.name: PayableStretchLeverageRisk
evaluated.expression: NEG(MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(apalch, cogs), 1)), RANK(RATIO(lt, at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Operating cash flow manufactured by stretching trade payables is the lowest-quality form of reported cash generation, and it is most dangerous in highly levered firms, where suppliers tightening terms can force an abrupt liquidity squeeze.
evaluated.reasoning: All prior accrual channels here were asset-side (receivables, inventory, cash, working capital); this is the first liability-side accrual mechanism, and it pairs with a solvency-based quality modifier rather than a profitability one. Scaling payable changes by cost of goods sold expresses the stretch in days-of-purchases terms, and the leverage rank concentrates the signal where a supplier-credit reversal is economically binding.

evaluated.name: FirmRelativeAccrualSurprise
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale), 5))), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What signals accounting noise is a departure from the firm's own accrual regime, not its position in the cross-section: a consistently profitable firm posting its highest non-cash working-capital build in five years is stretching recognition, whereas a firm whose accrual is low relative to its own history is reporting conservatively.
evaluated.reasoning: Cross-sectional scaling of accruals conflates business-model differences (distributors and manufacturers structurally carry more working capital) with reporting choices, and this replaces it with a within-firm historical position while holding the conditioner and structure of the archive's best signal constant. If the firm-relative version dominates, later generations should normalize accruals within firm rather than within the cross-section; if it fails, the effect is genuinely a cross-sectional level effect.

evaluated.name: ChronicConservatismRegime
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(dpc, DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), sale), 3), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Reporting conservatism is a persistent firm attribute, not an annual event: a firm whose income is habitually charged with depreciation rather than inflated by working-capital builds is running a conservative accounting regime, and among persistently profitable firms that regime marks earnings as genuinely cash-backed.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than stretching the differencing window (which turns the accrual into an asset-growth proxy), this changes the accrual construct itself — depreciation charged *minus* non-cash working-capital accrued, then averaged over three years to capture the regime rather than one year's flow — so a positive result attributes to reporting policy, not to growth. Industry z-scoring is essential here because `dpc/sale` embeds capital intensity, and it removes the sector component that a plain cross-sectional standardization would leave in the accrual leg.

evaluated.name: PayoutValidatedAccrualQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ni, DELTA(re, 1)), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The hardest available verification that reported income was real cash is that the firm distributed it: income minus the increase in retained earnings is cash returned to shareholders, and only firms that both avoid working-capital accrual builds and actually pay out are unambiguously cash-backed.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the cash-versus-retained-earnings wedge and replaces it with a payout-based validation channel — an economic mechanism absent from the archive — while keeping the accrual primitive that produced the archive's only doubly-significant result. It also re-tests the weakest-link conjunction, whose earlier failure is fully attributable to being paired with the inverted volatility channel, so pairing it with a validated quality channel is a genuine functional-form test rather than a respecification of a prior signal.

evaluated.name: IndustryRelativeAccrualStreak
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Required working capital is a technology, not a choice: distributors and manufacturers structurally carry receivables and inventory that service firms do not, so the accounting-noise component of an accrual is the part that deviates from the industry norm.
evaluated.reasoning: The only industry-adjusted signal tested so far had its accrual leg contaminated by `dpc` (capital intensity), which destroyed the FMB slope while preserving a 2.3 alpha t-stat; applying `IND_ZSCORE` to the clean, validated accrual primitive separates the industry-normalization question from the depreciation contamination. If it improves on both metrics, later generations should treat industry-relative scaling as the default for the accrual leg.

evaluated.name: AccrualReversalQuality
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale), 1)), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Mispricing arises at the moment the accounting regime turns: a persistently profitable firm whose working-capital accrual is decelerating is beginning to convert prior book earnings into cash, while one whose accrual is accelerating is entering the unbacked phase, and the market prices the level of accruals sooner than the change.
evaluated.reasoning: Every accrual construct in the archive is a level or a cumulative flow, so the change-in-accrual channel is an untested temporal mechanism that carries different economic content — reversal timing rather than accounting stock — and is close to orthogonal to the level sort, making it a candidate for combination later. Holding the conditioner and scaling fixed keeps the comparison against the archive's best signal interpretable.

evaluated.name: UnfundedAccrualBuild
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(che, 3))), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What makes a working-capital build dangerous is not its size relative to revenue but whether the firm has liquid resources to carry it: an accrual build that is large relative to the firm's own cash reserves must eventually be financed or liquidated, so it is the accrual-to-liquidity ratio that separates durable cash earnings from accounting noise.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than averaging two correlated normalizations of the same numerator, this changes the economic normalization itself — the deflator becomes the three-year average cash balance, so identical sales-scaled accruals score very differently depending on liquidity capacity, which no archive signal captures. The three-year averaging of `che` stabilizes a volatile denominator and winsorization plus z-scoring contain the small-cash tail before the persistence weight is applied.

evaluated.name: CostDisciplineCashBacking
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(cogs, revt), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable cash earnings come from operational improvement, not recognition timing: a firm whose unit cost ratio has been falling for five years is genuinely getting more efficient, and when that improvement is unaccompanied by a working-capital build the reported performance is real, while accrual-inflated earnings at firms with deteriorating cost ratios are the clearest accounting noise.
evaluated.reasoning: This introduces a cost-side quality channel that is economically distinct from the profitability level and profit-persistence conditioners already tested — it measures the direction of operating efficiency rather than the level or reliability of profit — so the outcome cannot be an interpolation of two prior archive results. It also avoids the banned second-moment channel while still using a multi-year window, since cost discipline is meaningful only as a trend.

evaluated.name: TaxCorroboratedAccrualPurity
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(txp, 1), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A working-capital build that is not accompanied by a rise in taxes owed is income recognized for shareholders but not for the tax authority; conversely, low accruals combined with growing tax obligations mean the reported profit is both cash-backed and independently corroborated by a third party with no interest in flattering the accounts.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the debt-financing conditioner, whose non-negative weight produced the sign incoherence the critic identified and which duplicated the net-issuance anomaly, with a book-tax corroboration weight whose two tails are both economically coherent: long leg is low-accrual firms with rising tax claims, short leg is accrual builders whose tax obligations are flat. The tax channel produced the only two positive alphas among the archive's non-accrual mechanisms, so embedding it as the conditioner of the validated accrual base tests a genuine complementarity rather than a blend of two accrual normalizations.

evaluated.name: DistributionsNetOfAccrualAbsorption
evaluated.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ni, DELTA(re, 1)), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), sale), 1)
evaluated.hypothesis: The economically complete measure of cash-backed reported performance is what the firm actually handed to shareholders minus what its operations absorbed into working capital; reported income that is neither distributed nor converted to cash is accounting noise regardless of how profitable the firm looks.
evaluated.reasoning: Instead of escalating corner purity with a third MIN hurdle, this fuses the payout channel and the accrual channel into one signed cash-flow identity — distributions less working-capital absorption per dollar of sales — so the signal is continuous, monotone and interpretable, which addresses the archive's evidence that MIN forms concentrate composition risk while flattening the cross-sectional slope. Because both components come from the same annual statements, coverage stays near the 0.11 of the validated family rather than falling to the sparse cash-flow-statement sample.

evaluated.name: UnfundedAccrualTaxCorroborated
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(che, 3))), 1)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(txp, 1), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The sharpest case of accounting noise is a working-capital build the firm cannot fund from its own cash *and* that generates no additional tax obligation: the earnings exist only in the books, are not corroborated by the tax authority, and cannot be carried without external financing.
evaluated.reasoning: This pairs the best-alpha conditioner with the best-t deflator, two axes whose economic content is independent — one measures capacity to carry the accrual, the other measures third-party verification of the income it produced. If the combination exceeds both parents, the two failure modes of low-quality earnings (unfundable and unverified) are distinct populations; if it merely interpolates, they are the same firms and later generations should pick one.

evaluated.name: ConstrainedFirmAccrualPricing
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(MA(che, 3), lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual mispricing is concentrated in financially constrained firms: when a cash-poor, liability-heavy firm inflates earnings with working-capital builds, the reversal forces real operating retrenchment, whereas a cash-rich firm can absorb the same build without consequence.
evaluated.reasoning: `UnfundedAccrualBuild` deflated the accrual by cash and produced the archive's most reliable alpha, but that construction conflates two stories — a scaling choice and a constraint interaction — and this separates them by keeping the validated sales-scaled accrual and moving liquidity into the conditioner as cash relative to total liabilities. Comparing the three liquidity signals identifies whether to build future signals around the ratio form or the conditioning form.

evaluated.name: AssetSideUnfundedAccrual
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), MA(che, 3))), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Only the asset side of working capital is genuinely unverifiable — receivables that may not be collected and inventory that may not sell — whereas operating liabilities are contractual amounts owed, so the earnings-quality content of the accrual should reside entirely in the non-cash current asset build.

evaluated.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ni, DELTA(re, 1)), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), sale), 1))
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash handed to shareholders net of cash absorbed by working capital is the completeness test of reported earnings, but payout policy is strongly industry-clustered, so the informative quantity is a firm's free-cash-to-owners relative to what is normal in its sector.

evaluated.name: CashDrainingAccrualBuild
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), DELTA(che, 1)), sale)), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What identifies an unfunded accrual is not the size of the cash buffer that could absorb it but whether the build actually drained the treasury: a firm whose working capital expanded while its cash balance simultaneously fell financed reported earnings by consuming liquidity, whereas a firm that grew working capital *and* cash generated real surplus.

evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ni, sale), 1))))

evaluated.name: AssetBuildConstrainedFirm

evaluated.name: ConcealedDeclineAssetBuild
