considered.name: SoftAccrualStabilityAmplified
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(recch, invch), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Receivable and inventory accruals are the least verifiable ("soft") components of earnings, and their information content is strongest for firms whose gross margins are otherwise stable, because in a stable-margin firm an unexplained soft-accrual build cannot be attributed to genuine operating turbulence.
considered.reasoning: The cash-flow-statement items enter with their native sign (cash released when receivables and inventories fall), so a high centered value means collections and inventory discipline, and the gross-margin stability rank acts as a continuous multiplicative weight rather than a hard gate that creates a mass point at zero. Because the accrual term is cross-sectionally centered, the weight steepens the slope on both tails for stable-margin firms and shrinks noisy, turbulent firms toward neutral.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TaxCorroboratedEarningsTrend
considered.expression: NEG(SUB(TREND(RATIO(ni, sale), 5), TREND(RATIO(txp, sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: A multi-year improvement in reported margins is only credible if it is corroborated by a parallel build in tax obligations; earnings trends unaccompanied by taxes owed reflect book-only accrual recognition that reverses.
considered.reasoning: This uses the tax-accrual channel as an external validator of the quality theme's earnings-persistence trend, an interaction with no counterpart in a standard accrual level sort. Firms whose margin trend runs far ahead of their tax-accrual trend are flagged as accounting-driven and should underperform, while firms whose taxes owed keep pace with reported margins have economically real income.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualSmoothingDetector
considered.expression: NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(VOL(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), sale), 5), VOL(RATIO(ni, sale), 5)), 1))
considered.hypothesis: Smooth reported earnings are a quality signal only when they are not manufactured: if working-capital accruals swing far more than reported margins, accruals are absorbing operating shocks and the apparent stability is an artifact of accounting discretion.
considered.reasoning: The ratio directly measures how much work the accrual process does per unit of reported earnings variability, so it separates naturally stable firms (low ratio, high signal) from smoothers whose earnings stability is purchased with volatile accruals. This attacks the theme interaction from the second-moment side rather than the level side, and therefore cannot be a repackaging of any accrual or earnings-volatility level sort.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: InventoryBuildVsDemand
considered.expression: NEG(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(NEG(invch), cogs), GROWTH(revt, 1)), 1))
considered.hypothesis: Inventory accumulation is only legitimate when it is matched by growing demand; a firm adding inventory equal to a rising fraction of its annual cost of sales while revenue stagnates is accruing future writedowns rather than building durable earnings power.
considered.reasoning: This drops apalch (which perversely rewarded payable stretching) and replaces the gross-profit denominator, whose sign flips for weak firms, with cogs — positive for essentially all operating firms — so the accrual is expressed as a change in days-of-inventory. The interaction is a genuine mismatch test between an accruals-exclusive stock build and the quality theme's revenue-growth base, not a rescaled accrual level: identical inventory builds score very differently depending on whether demand is expanding.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashBackedMarginTrendProduct
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(TREND(RATIO(ni, sale), 5)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), sale))))
considered.hypothesis: A multi-year improvement in net margin earns a return premium only when working capital is not absorbing the improvement; accrual-financed margin gains should be shorted, not treated as neutral, because they reverse as working capital unwinds.
considered.reasoning: Multiplying two non-negative goodness ranks makes the top of the distribution reachable only in the doubly-good corner (improving margins and released working capital), while accrual-heavy improvers have a near-zero accrual rank and therefore fall into the short leg rather than to a neutral midpoint — the exact sign defect flagged in the previous version. Against the accepted MIN-based signal it isolates two design choices at once: smooth product versus weakest-link conjunction, and margin trend versus margin volatility as the quality dimension.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualPurityProfitStreak
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Earnings persistence is better captured by an uninterrupted record of positive margins than by low margin volatility; low non-cash accruals are informative about durable cash earnings specifically for firms that have proven repeatedly that they can earn a profit at all.
considered.reasoning: The base is the cash-excluded accrual, centered so both tails are active, and the modifier is a continuous rank of the five-year count of profitable years, which avoids both the VOL channel that inverted in gen 1 and the zero mass point of a hard indicator gate. Paired with Signal 1, this isolates the quality-channel choice (persistence count versus volatility) while holding the repaired accrual primitive constant.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SoftAccrualDemandMismatchRank
considered.expression: SUB(RANK(GROWTH(revt, 1)), RANK(RATIO(NEG(ADD(recch, invch)), cogs)))
considered.hypothesis: Revenue expansion is high quality only when it is not absorbed into receivables and inventory; the informative variable is the *gap* between demand growth and soft-accrual build, and it should be measured in rank space because the raw ratio's tails, not its middle, drove the gen-1 result.
considered.reasoning: InventoryBuildVsDemand had the strongest FF5 alpha in the archive (t=2.30) but a wrong-signed FMB slope, the classic symptom of a raw-difference construction whose extreme values dominate the decile spread while the middle of the distribution is noisy or non-monotone. Converting both legs to cross-sectional ranks before differencing makes the relation monotone and comparable across firms, and adding receivables to inventory broadens the soft-accrual concept to the full operating cycle.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: MatureFirmCashConversion
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(recch, invch), sale), 1)), RANK(RATIO(re, at)))
considered.hypothesis: Working-capital accruals carry different information across the corporate life cycle: in a firm with a large stock of accumulated retained earnings, a receivables or inventory build is discretion rather than necessary growth financing, whereas in a young, low-retained-earnings firm the same build is the mechanical cost of expansion.
considered.reasoning: Retained earnings over assets is a durability/lifecycle proxy from the quality menu that is a level rather than a second moment, so it sidesteps the volatility channel that inverted, and it enters as a non-negative weight that steepens the accrual slope for seasoned firms and shrinks young firms toward neutral. This tests whether the accruals effect is concentrated in mature, self-financed firms — a conditioning story distinct from profitability persistence.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ChronicCashConversionMarginTrend
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(ADD(recch, invch), sale), 5)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: A single year of cash-favorable working-capital flows is noise; five years of cumulative cash release combined with an improving gross margin identifies firms whose reported improvement is structurally cash-backed rather than accrual-financed.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the accrual *level* with a five-year cumulative flow, a persistence concept, and pairs it conjunctively with a margin *trend* so the long leg requires both chronic cash conversion and genuine profitability improvement. It tests whether the accruals x quality interaction is a slow-moving regime property rather than an annual event, which would also explain the weak annual-level FMB slopes seen so far.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TaxCorroborationConjunction
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(TREND(RATIO(ni, sale), 5)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(txp, sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Rising reported margins are credible only when tax obligations rise alongside them; requiring both trends to be high simultaneously identifies firms whose book income improvement is corroborated by the tax authorities' claim on it.
considered.reasoning: The gen-1 difference-of-trends version produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.195) and a positive alpha but also awarded top scores to the economically incoherent case of falling margins with rising taxes payable; the weakest-link conjunction removes that contamination from the long leg while preserving the corroboration mechanism. Because both legs are trends of levels scaled by sales, this also keeps the coverage profile of the gen-1 version rather than trading evidence for a sparser sample.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashAccumulationVsBookProfit
considered.expression: SUB(RANK(RATIO(DELTA(che, 3), sale)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(re, 3), sale)))
considered.hypothesis: Genuinely cash-backed profits eventually show up as a build in the cash balance, so over a multi-year window the accumulation of retained earnings should be tracked by the accumulation of cash; firms whose book profits pile up in retained earnings without any corresponding cash build are reporting accounting profit that never became spendable resources.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the rejected MIN-of-two-published-anomalies structure entirely and replaces both legs: the accruals channel is now the change in the cash stock itself (`che`, an accruals-exclusive primitive never used so far), and the quality channel is the accumulation of retained profits (`re`), so the signal is a stock-level corroboration test rather than a flow-accrual sort combined with earnings smoothness. The three-year differencing horizon smooths one-off financing and dividend timing, and rank differencing keeps the comparison monotone and scale-free, addressing the raw-difference tail sensitivity seen in gen 1.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualPurityGrossProfit
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Cash-purged low accruals identify durable earnings specifically among firms with genuine operating profitability; for firms whose gross profit per unit of assets is weak, accrual conservatism reflects shrinking operations rather than cash-backed performance.
considered.reasoning: This keeps the archive's only doubly-significant accrual primitive fixed and replaces the coarse six-valued profit streak with a continuous gross-profitability rank, directly answering the critic's concern that the conditioner's granularity limited the interaction. Gross profitability is a level, not a second moment, so it avoids the volatility channel that inverted four times in gen 1, and the comparison against the streak version isolates whether the conditioning content is profitability *magnitude* or profitability *reliability*.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DebtFinancedAccrualBuild
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(dltt, 1), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual quality matters most where the accrual is externally financed: a working-capital build funded by new long-term borrowing commits the firm to fixed claims against earnings that have not yet converted to cash, so accrual reversal turns into genuine financial stress rather than a harmless accounting unwind.
considered.reasoning: This introduces the financing side of the balance sheet (`dltt`) as the quality modifier, an economic channel absent from the archive, and it amplifies the accrual slope symmetrically — debt-financed accrual builders sit in the short leg while cash-backed firms that can still access debt markets sit in the long leg. It tests a distinct hypothesis about *why* the interaction exists (financing fragility) rather than *who* has quality earnings (profitability).
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PayableStretchLeverageRisk
considered.expression: NEG(MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(apalch, cogs), 1)), RANK(RATIO(lt, at))))
considered.hypothesis: Operating cash flow manufactured by stretching trade payables is the lowest-quality form of reported cash generation, and it is most dangerous in highly levered firms, where suppliers tightening terms can force an abrupt liquidity squeeze.
considered.reasoning: All prior accrual channels here were asset-side (receivables, inventory, cash, working capital); this is the first liability-side accrual mechanism, and it pairs with a solvency-based quality modifier rather than a profitability one. Scaling payable changes by cost of goods sold expresses the stretch in days-of-purchases terms, and the leverage rank concentrates the signal where a supplier-credit reversal is economically binding.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FirmRelativeAccrualSurprise
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale), 5))), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: What signals accounting noise is a departure from the firm's own accrual regime, not its position in the cross-section: a consistently profitable firm posting its highest non-cash working-capital build in five years is stretching recognition, whereas a firm whose accrual is low relative to its own history is reporting conservatively.
considered.reasoning: Cross-sectional scaling of accruals conflates business-model differences (distributors and manufacturers structurally carry more working capital) with reporting choices, and this replaces it with a within-firm historical position while holding the conditioner and structure of the archive's best signal constant. If the firm-relative version dominates, later generations should normalize accruals within firm rather than within the cross-section; if it fails, the effect is genuinely a cross-sectional level effect.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ChronicConservatismRegime
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(SUB(dpc, DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), sale), 3), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Reporting conservatism is a persistent firm attribute, not an annual event: a firm whose income is habitually charged with depreciation rather than inflated by working-capital builds is running a conservative accounting regime, and among persistently profitable firms that regime marks earnings as genuinely cash-backed.
considered.reasoning: Rather than stretching the differencing window (which turns the accrual into an asset-growth proxy), this changes the accrual construct itself — depreciation charged *minus* non-cash working-capital accrued, then averaged over three years to capture the regime rather than one year's flow — so a positive result attributes to reporting policy, not to growth. Industry z-scoring is essential here because `dpc/sale` embeds capital intensity, and it removes the sector component that a plain cross-sectional standardization would leave in the accrual leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PayoutValidatedAccrualQuality
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ni, DELTA(re, 1)), sale)))
considered.hypothesis: The hardest available verification that reported income was real cash is that the firm distributed it: income minus the increase in retained earnings is cash returned to shareholders, and only firms that both avoid working-capital accrual builds and actually pay out are unambiguously cash-backed.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the cash-versus-retained-earnings wedge and replaces it with a payout-based validation channel — an economic mechanism absent from the archive — while keeping the accrual primitive that produced the archive's only doubly-significant result. It also re-tests the weakest-link conjunction, whose earlier failure is fully attributable to being paired with the inverted volatility channel, so pairing it with a validated quality channel is a genuine functional-form test rather than a respecification of a prior signal.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: IndustryRelativeAccrualStreak
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Required working capital is a technology, not a choice: distributors and manufacturers structurally carry receivables and inventory that service firms do not, so the accounting-noise component of an accrual is the part that deviates from the industry norm.
considered.reasoning: The only industry-adjusted signal tested so far had its accrual leg contaminated by `dpc` (capital intensity), which destroyed the FMB slope while preserving a 2.3 alpha t-stat; applying `IND_ZSCORE` to the clean, validated accrual primitive separates the industry-normalization question from the depreciation contamination. If it improves on both metrics, later generations should treat industry-relative scaling as the default for the accrual leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AccrualReversalQuality
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale), 1)), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Mispricing arises at the moment the accounting regime turns: a persistently profitable firm whose working-capital accrual is decelerating is beginning to convert prior book earnings into cash, while one whose accrual is accelerating is entering the unbacked phase, and the market prices the level of accruals sooner than the change.
considered.reasoning: Every accrual construct in the archive is a level or a cumulative flow, so the change-in-accrual channel is an untested temporal mechanism that carries different economic content — reversal timing rather than accounting stock — and is close to orthogonal to the level sort, making it a candidate for combination later. Holding the conditioner and scaling fixed keeps the comparison against the archive's best signal interpretable.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: UnfundedAccrualBuild
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(che, 3))), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: What makes a working-capital build dangerous is not its size relative to revenue but whether the firm has liquid resources to carry it: an accrual build that is large relative to the firm's own cash reserves must eventually be financed or liquidated, so it is the accrual-to-liquidity ratio that separates durable cash earnings from accounting noise.
considered.reasoning: Rather than averaging two correlated normalizations of the same numerator, this changes the economic normalization itself — the deflator becomes the three-year average cash balance, so identical sales-scaled accruals score very differently depending on liquidity capacity, which no archive signal captures. The three-year averaging of `che` stabilizes a volatile denominator and winsorization plus z-scoring contain the small-cash tail before the persistence weight is applied.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CostDisciplineCashBacking
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(cogs, revt), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Durable cash earnings come from operational improvement, not recognition timing: a firm whose unit cost ratio has been falling for five years is genuinely getting more efficient, and when that improvement is unaccompanied by a working-capital build the reported performance is real, while accrual-inflated earnings at firms with deteriorating cost ratios are the clearest accounting noise.
considered.reasoning: This introduces a cost-side quality channel that is economically distinct from the profitability level and profit-persistence conditioners already tested — it measures the direction of operating efficiency rather than the level or reliability of profit — so the outcome cannot be an interpolation of two prior archive results. It also avoids the banned second-moment channel while still using a multi-year window, since cost discipline is meaningful only as a trend.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TaxCorroboratedAccrualPurity
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(txp, 1), sale)))
considered.hypothesis: A working-capital build that is not accompanied by a rise in taxes owed is income recognized for shareholders but not for the tax authority; conversely, low accruals combined with growing tax obligations mean the reported profit is both cash-backed and independently corroborated by a third party with no interest in flattering the accounts.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the debt-financing conditioner, whose non-negative weight produced the sign incoherence the critic identified and which duplicated the net-issuance anomaly, with a book-tax corroboration weight whose two tails are both economically coherent: long leg is low-accrual firms with rising tax claims, short leg is accrual builders whose tax obligations are flat. The tax channel produced the only two positive alphas among the archive's non-accrual mechanisms, so embedding it as the conditioner of the validated accrual base tests a genuine complementarity rather than a blend of two accrual normalizations.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DistributionsNetOfAccrualAbsorption
considered.expression: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ni, DELTA(re, 1)), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), sale), 1)
considered.hypothesis: The economically complete measure of cash-backed reported performance is what the firm actually handed to shareholders minus what its operations absorbed into working capital; reported income that is neither distributed nor converted to cash is accounting noise regardless of how profitable the firm looks.
considered.reasoning: Instead of escalating corner purity with a third MIN hurdle, this fuses the payout channel and the accrual channel into one signed cash-flow identity — distributions less working-capital absorption per dollar of sales — so the signal is continuous, monotone and interpretable, which addresses the archive's evidence that MIN forms concentrate composition risk while flattening the cross-sectional slope. Because both components come from the same annual statements, coverage stays near the 0.11 of the validated family rather than falling to the sparse cash-flow-statement sample.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: UnfundedAccrualTaxCorroborated
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), MA(che, 3))), 1)), RANK(RATIO(DELTA(txp, 1), sale)))
considered.hypothesis: The sharpest case of accounting noise is a working-capital build the firm cannot fund from its own cash *and* that generates no additional tax obligation: the earnings exist only in the books, are not corroborated by the tax authority, and cannot be carried without external financing.
considered.reasoning: This pairs the best-alpha conditioner with the best-t deflator, two axes whose economic content is independent — one measures capacity to carry the accrual, the other measures third-party verification of the income it produced. If the combination exceeds both parents, the two failure modes of low-quality earnings (unfundable and unverified) are distinct populations; if it merely interpolates, they are the same firms and later generations should pick one.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ConstrainedFirmAccrualPricing
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(MA(che, 3), lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual mispricing is concentrated in financially constrained firms: when a cash-poor, liability-heavy firm inflates earnings with working-capital builds, the reversal forces real operating retrenchment, whereas a cash-rich firm can absorb the same build without consequence.
considered.reasoning: `UnfundedAccrualBuild` deflated the accrual by cash and produced the archive's most reliable alpha, but that construction conflates two stories — a scaling choice and a constraint interaction — and this separates them by keeping the validated sales-scaled accrual and moving liquidity into the conditioner as cash relative to total liabilities. Comparing the three liquidity signals identifies whether to build future signals around the ratio form or the conditioning form.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AssetSideUnfundedAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), MA(che, 3))), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Only the asset side of working capital is genuinely unverifiable — receivables that may not be collected and inventory that may not sell — whereas operating liabilities are contractual amounts owed, so the earnings-quality content of the accrual should reside entirely in the non-cash current asset build.
considered.reasoning: The archive contains conflicting evidence on the liability side: `PayableStretchLeverageRisk` produced a significantly *negative* alpha, implying payable increases are return-enhancing in a way that may or may not be captured correctly by netting them inside the accrual. Isolating the asset-side build against the same liquidity deflator and conditioner determines whether the liability leg adds information or merely adds noise, which directly informs the primitive used in the final generations.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: IndustryFreeCashToOwners
considered.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ni, DELTA(re, 1)), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), sale), 1))
considered.hypothesis: Cash handed to shareholders net of cash absorbed by working capital is the completeness test of reported earnings, but payout policy is strongly industry-clustered, so the informative quantity is a firm's free-cash-to-owners relative to what is normal in its sector.
considered.reasoning: The raw version earned a credible 2.8% alpha (t 2.87) but a weak FMB slope of 1.64, the signature of a cross-sectional distribution dominated by sector-level payout regimes rather than firm-level cash backing, which is precisely the contamination `IND_ZSCORE` removed elsewhere in this archive. This targets the specific diagnosed weakness of an existing mechanism instead of adding hurdles or conditioners to it.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashDrainingAccrualBuild
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), DELTA(che, 1)), sale)), 1)), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: What identifies an unfunded accrual is not the size of the cash buffer that could absorb it but whether the build actually drained the treasury: a firm whose working capital expanded while its cash balance simultaneously fell financed reported earnings by consuming liquidity, whereas a firm that grew working capital *and* cash generated real surplus.
considered.reasoning: This is a flow-versus-flow construction — contemporaneous accrual build netted against contemporaneous treasury accumulation — rather than the stock-deflator scaling of `UnfundedAccrualBuild`, so it tests the funding *event* instead of funding *capacity* and can succeed or fail independently of its predecessor. It also avoids the redundancy problem of stacking IND_ZSCORE on an already-validated parent, because the numerator itself is a different economic quantity rather than the same numerator rescaled.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DecliningEarningsAccrualIncentive
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ni, sale), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Accruals are informative in proportion to management's incentive to use them: when margins are deteriorating, a working-capital build is very likely an attempt to conceal the decline, whereas the same build in an improving year is more plausibly operational, so the accrual signal should be steepest among firms whose profitability just fell.
considered.reasoning: Every conditioner tested so far is a "good-quality" weight (profitability level, persistence, cost discipline, tax corroboration) that concentrates the signal among strong firms; this inverts the logic and conditions on *incentive intensity*, so the long leg is firms that reported an honest margin decline without inflating working capital and the short leg is firms that hid a decline behind an accrual build. It is a behavioural conditioning mechanism rather than a symbolic restatement of a published discretionary-accrual model, and it uses only annual balance-sheet and income items so coverage stays at the family's ~0.11.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AssetBuildConstrainedFirm
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(MA(che, 3), lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Durable cash earnings require both that reported profit not be parked in unverifiable current assets and that the firm could survive the reversal if it were; the interaction is means (an asset-side build) times consequence (no liquid buffer against the claims on the firm).
considered.reasoning: The two strongest archive results identified the asset-side numerator and the liquidity-constraint conditioner separately, and this pairs them while deliberately deflating by sales rather than cash so that `che` does not appear on both sides of the product — the redundancy that would make the interaction mechanically self-referential. If it exceeds both parents on alpha and slope, the accrual measure and the reversal-cost measure are capturing genuinely different economics rather than the same constrained-firm population.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ConcealedDeclineAssetBuild
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), MA(che, 3))), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ni, sale), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Accounting noise is most detectable when means and motive coincide: a firm whose margin just fell and which simultaneously financed an unverifiable current-asset build beyond its cash resources is concealing deterioration, while a firm that reported the decline honestly and kept its asset base clean has genuinely cash-backed, if unexciting, earnings.
considered.reasoning: This pairs the archive's best-slope accrual primitive with the incentive conditioner rather than with another quality or constraint measure, so the two legs come from different economic families — capacity/verifiability on one side, managerial motive on the other — which is the combination most likely to add information rather than interpolate. Both parents were individually strong on alpha and slope, and neither shares an input with the other, so a joint improvement would be attributable to the interaction itself.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AssetBuildIntoSlowingDemand
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(GROWTH(revt, 1), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: An unverifiable current-asset build is benign when demand is accelerating and toxic when demand is decelerating: receivables extended to weakening customers and inventory built into a slowing order book are the accruals that fail to convert to cash and eventually get written down.
considered.reasoning: Instead of spending the slot on a pure deflator ablation of an existing signal, this pairs the validated asset-side accrual with a demand-deceleration conditioner that is new to the archive — every prior conditioner measured profitability, taxes, liquidity or margin direction, none measured the second derivative of revenue. The economic content is the realizability of the asset build, which is precisely the reliability question the accrual literature raises but does not condition on.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: NetIndebtedAccrualPricing
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(lt, che), at)))
considered.hypothesis: The capacity to absorb an accrual reversal is governed by claims net of liquid assets: a firm whose liabilities exceed its cash by a large fraction of its asset base has no slack, whereas a net-cash firm can write down receivables or inventory without consequence.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the badly behaved `lt/ceq` conditioner — negative and near-zero book equity would have ranked the most fragile firms at the wrong end — with net debt over assets, which is finite and monotone for every firm including those with impaired equity. Against the parent conditioner (cash over total liabilities) it isolates whether reversal-absorption capacity is better measured by liquid resources alone or by liabilities net of liquidity relative to firm size.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: JustProfitableAccrualScrutiny
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), MUL(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ni, sale)))))
considered.hypothesis: The benchmark-beating incentive is asymmetric and applies only to firms that reported a profit: among profitable firms, the thinner the margin the greater the temptation to have manufactured it through working-capital recognition, so accruals are most diagnostic of accounting noise for barely-profitable firms and least diagnostic for comfortably profitable ones.
considered.reasoning: The previous version used `NEG(ABS(ni/sale))`, which weighted small losses identically to small profits and loaded on low profitability generally; the indicator now switches the scrutiny weight on only for profitable firms and the rank makes it decline in margin size, so the weight peaks just above zero exactly as the threshold story requires. Loss-making firms receive a neutral zero weight, which is the intended economics — a firm that reported a loss did not use accruals to beat the zero benchmark — and this keeps the signal consistent with the archive's finding that the effect lives among profitable firms.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ChronicWorkingCapitalDrift
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(NEG(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)), 0), 5))), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: A single year in which unverifiable current assets outgrow sales is operational noise, but a firm that has done so in most of the last five years is running a deteriorating recognition regime in which reported profits chronically fail to convert into cash.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the equity-deflator idea, whose negative and near-zero denominators the critic correctly identified as fatal, and replaces it with a frequency construct: the count of years in which asset-side working capital grew faster than revenue, which is scale-free, sign-stable and requires no deflator at all. Frequency of efficiency deterioration is a persistence concept untested in the archive — distinct from the level, the change and the cumulative flow — and conditioning it on the profit streak keeps the interaction inside the validated quality channel.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ThinMarginSurvivorAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(ni, sale))), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: The firms whose accruals reveal the most are those that have never reported a loss yet operate on razor-thin margins: their record creates the expectation of continued profitability while their margin gives them almost no real cushion to deliver it honestly.
considered.reasoning: This repairs the diagnosed defect of `JustProfitableAccrualScrutiny` — a hard indicator zeroed roughly a quarter of the cross-section, creating a mass point at zero that flattened the FMB slope to 1.48 despite a 4.97 alpha t-stat — by replacing the discontinuous gate with a continuous weakest-link of thin margin and profit persistence, which is strictly positive for every firm. If the alpha survives while the slope rises, the threshold mechanism is real and the previous weak slope was purely a distributional artifact.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ShortDatedClaimsAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dltt, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Fragility is about timing as well as quantity: a firm whose obligations are predominantly short-dated must refinance before an inflated working-capital position can unwind, so accrual-supported earnings are most dangerous where little of the liability structure is long-term.
considered.reasoning: Both validated fragility conditioners measure the *size* of claims relative to liquid assets or total assets; claim maturity is an orthogonal dimension of the same economics and is untested in this archive, using only well-behaved non-negative ratios of reported liabilities. If it performs comparably, fragility conditioning is robust to proxy choice rather than an artifact of the cash variable, which matters because `che` currently appears in nearly every strong signal.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FullAccrualSlowingDemand
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(GROWTH(revt, 1), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: A working-capital build into decelerating demand signals inventory and receivables that will not convert, but the informative accrual must include operating liabilities, since payables move with the same demand cycle and omitting them leaves a growth-scale artifact rather than a reliability measure.
considered.reasoning: `AssetBuildIntoSlowingDemand` produced fmb 3.53 with a *negative* alpha, and `AssetBuildConstrainedFirm` did the same, so the negative-alpha failure is common to the asset-side-plus-sales numerator rather than to any one conditioner — this holds the demand conditioner fixed and restores the validated full-accrual numerator to test that attribution directly. The answer determines whether the demand-deceleration channel is usable at all in the final generation or should be discarded.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BarelyAvoidedDeclineAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), MUL(INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(ni, sale), 1), 0), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ni, sale), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: The second reporting benchmark managers protect is last year's earnings: a firm whose margin improved by the barest possible margin is the prime suspect for having closed the gap with working-capital recognition, while a firm that posted a clean improvement did not need to.
considered.reasoning: The archive now supports threshold-based conditioning at the zero-profit benchmark (α 4.4%, t 4.97) and direction-based conditioning on margin declines (α 2.9%, t 3.19); this tests the third possibility — the *change* benchmark at its threshold — which distinguishes whether the incentive effect is about the level of profit or about avoiding a reported deterioration. It reuses no fragility or liquidity input, so it also serves as an independent check that the strong incentive results are not proxying for balance-sheet weakness.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FragileThinMarginSurvivorAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(ni, at))), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(ni, 0), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: The accrual is maximally informative where means, motive and consequence coincide: a claims-heavy firm earning a thin but unbroken profit has the strongest incentive to sustain the record through working-capital recognition and the least capacity to absorb the reversal when it comes.
considered.reasoning: The hard `INDICATOR` gate is removed and replaced by a continuous weakest-link of claims intensity, thin return on assets and profit persistence, so no firm receives a zero weight and the mass point that flattened the FMB slope of `JustProfitableAccrualScrutiny` cannot recur. The conditioner is now built entirely from `lt`, `ni` and `at`, eliminating the shared-input problem the critic identified: `che` appears only in the accrual numerator and `sale` only as its deflator.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: WorkingCapitalStockAtOwnHigh
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5))), RANK(RATIO(lt, at)))
considered.hypothesis: A firm carrying its heaviest working-capital position in five years relative to its own sales base has accumulated unconverted claims beyond its own operating norm, and where the balance sheet is claims-heavy that overhang must be liquidated or written down rather than harmlessly carried.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the cross-sectional level with a within-firm historical position removes exactly the business-model variation that makes the raw working-capital-to-sales level a restatement of the published net-operating-assets sort — a distributor at its own five-year low scores well here while ranking poorly on the cross-sectional measure. The conditioner is switched to claims-to-assets so that `che` no longer appears on both sides, keeping the fragility channel independent of the accrual construct.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: StockOverhangThinMargin
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5))), MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(ni, sale))), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: A firm carrying its heaviest working-capital position in five years while reporting a thin but unbroken profit has both an accumulated overhang of unconverted claims and the strongest motive to keep deferring its recognition, so the two effects should compound.
considered.reasoning: The own-history stock base produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.415) and a 3.49 slope but only 2.3% alpha when paired with a leverage conditioner, while the thin-margin/survivor conditioner produced 4.2% alpha with a lower Sharpe — pairing them tests whether the alpha shortfall was the conditioner rather than the base. The two legs share no inputs beyond the sales deflator and target different economics (accumulated overhang versus reporting incentive).
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: NetIndebtedThinMarginAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(lt, che), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ni, sale)))))
considered.hypothesis: Motive and consequence together define the informative population: a thin-margin firm carrying heavy net debt has the strongest reason to inflate working capital and the least capacity to survive the reversal.
considered.reasoning: The two conditioners that each independently delivered 4.4% alpha come from separate economic families, and the archive's triple-leg experiment showed that stacking three legs dilutes (2.9%), so this tests the two-leg pairing that the dilution evidence implies is the right size. The `che` overlap with the numerator is not mechanical — the numerator uses the first difference of working capital while the conditioner uses the cash *level* net of liabilities — but the comparison against both parents will show whether the pairing adds beyond either.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: DiscretionCapacityAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale)))
considered.hypothesis: Accounting discretion requires a balance sheet to exercise it on: a firm whose operating cycle ties up a large stock of receivables and inventory per dollar of sales has far more room to shift recognition across periods than an asset-light firm, so identical accrual flows carry more information there.
considered.reasoning: Every conditioner tested so far measures profitability, incentive, financing fragility or demand — none measures the firm's *capacity* for accrual discretion, which is the necessary condition for the mechanism to operate at all. The conditioner is a positive, well-behaved ratio available for every firm, and if it works it identifies where to look for the effect independently of whether the firm is profitable, levered or under pressure.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: IndustryAccrualThinMarginSurvivor
considered.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(ni, sale))), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Required working capital is an industry technology while reporting pressure is a firm attribute, so the accounting-noise component of the accrual should be measured relative to sector norms and then priced most heavily among thin-margin firms with an unbroken profit record.
considered.reasoning: Industry demeaning of the accrual leg raised the slope from 2.08 to 3.12 and the Sharpe from 0.174 to 0.322 when paired with the streak conditioner, and the thin-margin/survivor conditioner independently lifted alpha to 4.2% with the plain cross-sectional base — the two improvements act on different components of the same product, so this is the strongest remaining untested combination. It is also the natural candidate to carry into the final generation if it delivers both the slope of the industry-adjusted family and the alpha of the incentive family.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BelowOwnNormThinMarginAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), MIN(RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(ni, sale), 3), RATIO(ni, sale))), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Reporting pressure is greatest for a firm that has never missed a profit yet is currently earning below its own three-year norm: the record sets the expectation and the shortfall creates the temptation to close the gap through working-capital recognition.
considered.reasoning: The critic is right that ranking the negative current margin against the ranked three-year average margin is a conjunction of two anticorrelated legs that selects mid-margin firms; expressing the idea as an explicit *difference* — the firm's own three-year average margin minus its current margin — computes the shortfall directly, and its rank is close to independent of the profit-streak leg so MIN now encodes the intended joint condition. This preserves the archive's validated structure (full-NWC accrual, two-leg continuous conditioner) while making the conditioner state firm-relative rather than cross-sectional.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: IndustryRelativeThinMarginSurvivor
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ni, sale))), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Margin thinness only signals reporting pressure relative to industry economics — a 3% net margin is precarious for a software firm and comfortable for a grocer — so the pressured population must be identified within industry while the profitability record remains an absolute test.
considered.reasoning: This now changes exactly one operator relative to the archive champion `ThinMarginSurvivorAccrual` — cross-sectional to industry ranking of the thin-margin leg — so any change in slope or alpha is attributable solely to industry-relative thinness rather than confounded with a second conditioner substitution. The economic case is that cross-sectional margin ranking mechanically loads the scrutiny weight onto structurally low-margin sectors instead of onto firms thin for their own business model.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: IncrementPlusOverhangAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5)))), MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(ni, sale))), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: This year's working-capital increment and the accumulated overhang relative to the firm's own history are economically distinct exposures — the flow measures current recognition aggressiveness, the stock measures how much unconverted claim is already on the books — and a firm that is high on both has the least cash-backed reported performance.
considered.reasoning: The archive shows these two bases behave differently under the identical conditioner (flow: α 4.2%, Sharpe 0.320; stock: α 3.0%, Sharpe 0.359, fmb 3.53), which is direct evidence that they are not redundant normalizations of one quantity but different economic objects. Combining them before conditioning tests whether the flow's alpha and the stock's slope stability can be held simultaneously, which no single-base signal in the archive has achieved.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FirmRelativeFlowThinMargin
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale), 5))), MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(ni, sale))), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual aggressiveness should be judged against the firm's own accounting history rather than against firms with different business models, and this within-firm departure is most informative among thin-margin firms with an unbroken profit record.
considered.reasoning: Three bases now exist — cross-sectional flow, firm-relative flow, and firm-relative stock — but the firm-relative flow has only ever been tested with the coarse profit-streak conditioner (fmb 2.97, α 2.1%, Sharpe 0.257), never with the thin-margin pair that lifted the cross-sectional flow to 4.2%. Completing this three-by-one grid settles which normalization the mechanism actually lives in, and the firm-relative version has the additional practical merit of being immune to industry composition drift.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AssetTiedCapacityAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, che), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Recognition discretion requires a balance sheet to exercise it on: the larger the share of a firm's total assets locked in receivables and inventory, the more room management has to shift income across periods and the more of the reported profit is exposed to eventual write-down.
considered.reasoning: The mislabeled "motive" leg is removed entirely — `RANK(NEG(ni/sale))` peaks for large losses rather than thin positive margins, so it does not implement the incentive story without a profitability gate — leaving a single, cleanly interpretable capacity conditioner. Deflating capacity by total assets rather than sales breaks the shared scaling with the base's sales deflator, so the interaction can no longer be a re-weighting of the accrual by its own denominator, which is the precise ambiguity the critic raised about `DiscretionCapacityAccrual`.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: StockOverhangShortDatedClaims
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), sale), 5))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dltt, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: An accumulated working-capital overhang is dangerous when it must be unwound faster than the firm's obligations allow: a firm at its own five-year peak of unconverted claims whose liabilities are predominantly short-dated must refinance before the overhang can convert to cash.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the verbatim borrowed two-leg conditioner — whose legs were both correlated with each other and contaminated by loss firms — with a single maturity-structure conditioner that is orthogonal to profitability and contains no cash or margin term, so nothing in the conditioner duplicates the base. The pairing is economically specific rather than a grid fill: the stock base measures how much must unwind, claim maturity measures how much time the firm has to unwind it.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AssetDeflatedAccrualThinMargin
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at)), 1)), MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(ni, sale))), RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, sale), 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: The economically correct scale for a working-capital accrual is the asset base that must absorb its reversal rather than the year's revenue, because two firms with identical sales but very different asset intensity face different consequences from the same unbacked build.
considered.reasoning: Swapping the conditioner's deflator from sales to cost of goods sold would indeed have been near-cosmetic given their proportionality, so the test is moved to the side where it actually bites: every accrual base in this archive has been deflated by sales, cash, or nothing, and the total-asset deflator — the standard in the accruals literature and never once evaluated here — is the one remaining normalization that could change the ranking materially. Pairing it with the validated thin-margin/unbroken-profit conditioner keeps everything else fixed so the deflator effect is cleanly attributable.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: UnverifiedThinMarginAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), sale)), 1)), MIN(RANK(NEG(RATIO(ni, sale))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(txp, 1), sale)))))
considered.hypothesis: Reported profit that is thin and generates no additional claim from the tax authority has passed no external verification, and it is exactly in that population that the working-capital accrual separates genuine cash-backed earnings from accounting noise.
considered.reasoning: The supplier-credit conditioner is abandoned because a fall in payables is equally consistent with strength, contraction, or monitoring — it was not identified — and it is replaced with the tax channel, the archive's one genuinely external corroboration source, which produced a 3.4% alpha as a standalone conditioner. Combining absent tax corroboration with thin margins gives a two-leg conjunction whose legs come from different information sources (internal incentive, external verification) and neither of which duplicates the accrual numerator.

critic_notes.rationale: This is an additive kitchen-sink of three separately published effects (Sloan accruals, earnings volatility, cash-margin trend) with no interaction mechanism, and the nested SUMRANK silently gives the accrual leg 50% weight versus 25% each for the other two, so any result will be hard to attribute and largely a repackaged accrual sort.

The conditioning logic is coherent and the sign is consistent, but zeroing out gated firms creates a large mass point at exactly zero that will sit mid-distribution and distort quantile breakpoints — a within-eligible-sample rank or a comparison against the ungated accrual baseline is needed for the test to be interpretable.

The OCF-per-unit-of-absolute-accrual ratio is a genuinely non-standard scale-free construction rather than a relabeled Sloan sort, though ordering will be dominated by near-zero denominators and by sign flips for negative-OCF firms, so winsorization at 1% is unlikely to be sufficient and coverage/stability diagnostics deserve close attention.

The stated mechanism fails the expression: a product of [0,1] ranks is small whenever *either* rank is small, so the long leg pools low-accrual/high-volatility and high-accrual/low-volatility firms with the "doubly-good" corner rather than concentrating on it, and the construction remains monotone in both inputs rather than isolating the claimed interaction.

Recasting accruals as a five-year count of cash-surplus years is a substantively different framing from the standard level sort and pairs sensibly with ROE stability; the main risks are the coarse 0–5 integer ties in one leg of the SUMRANK and negative-book-equity contamination in ni/ceq.

The accrual leg is Sloan (1996) essentially verbatim (ΔNWC less depreciation over assets), and industry-adjusting it and adding cash-flow volatility is a well-trodden refinement rather than a new cross-theme mechanism, so this is a rediscovery with cosmetic packaging.

The min-of-ranks conjunction is internally consistent and sign-coherent, but it is a fairly mechanical AND-combination of two well-known anomalies (working-capital accruals and earnings-volatility/stability) whose min operator discards the non-binding dimension's information, and the reasoning oddly cites an "earlier product-of-badness structure" that does not exist in this (empty) archive.

The construction is internally consistent — cash-flow-statement receivable/inventory items enter with native (cash-inflow-positive) sign, the centered z-score times a non-negative stability rank genuinely steepens both tails and shrinks turbulent firms toward neutral as claimed — though "soft"/percent accruals scaled by sales is close to published percent-accrual work and the incremental content rests entirely on the margin-stability weight.

Signs and hypothesis line up and the trend-divergence framing is a reasonable twist on the book-tax-difference literature, but the raw difference of two trends also awards top scores to firms with falling margins and rising taxes payable (an economically incoherent long-leg member), and txp is a noisy balance-sheet stock proxy for tax obligations.

Attacking the interaction through second moments is a genuinely different angle and the sign is coherent, but the construct is essentially the inverse of the established earnings-smoothness ratio (σ(accruals)/σ(earnings)) from the earnings-quality literature, and the denominator vanishes precisely for the smoothest firms, so results may be driven by winsorized division blowups rather than smoothing.

This is close to a repackaging of cash-based operating profitability (accruals subtracted from profit, here divided instead of subtracted), it is not really a cross-theme interaction but a rescaled accrual level, including apalch rewards payable stretching in contradiction to the stated hypothesis, and negative or near-zero gross profit flips the ratio's sign for exactly the firms where it matters.

The expression contradicts its own stated mechanism: multiplying a signed trend z-score by a non-negative accrual rank sends accrual-heavy improvers to ≈0 (neutral, not the short leg) while the short leg fills with cash-disciplined margin decliners, and the claimed "role reversal" of the earlier proposal is inaccurate since that signal used margin volatility, not margin trend.

This is the gen-1 WeakestLinkCashDiscipline expression with a single input swapped (wcap → non-cash net working capital), so it is largely a diagnostic rerun of an already-rejected structure whose two legs are each textbook published anomalies (Sloan accruals and earnings smoothness) with no new economic content beyond the measurement fix.

Internally consistent (signed non-cash accrual base times a non-negative persistence weight, positive sign matches the Sloan direction) and it substitutes a genuinely different quality channel for the failed volatility channel, but the profit-streak modifier takes only six distinct values so the conditioning is coarse and the composite is close in spirit to Piotroski's accrual-plus-profitability screen.

The rank-space differencing is a well-motivated response to the specific FMB/alpha sign conflict in InventoryBuildVsDemand rather than a cosmetic tweak, the sign convention on recch/invch is consistent with the archive's usage, and broadening inventory to the full operating cycle is a substantive change — though the resulting "growth minus working-capital build" spread overlaps meaningfully with known inventory-growth and net-operating-asset anomalies.

A coherent level-based lifecycle conditioner that avoids the inverted second-moment channel and is directionally consistent with the expression, but RE/AT is itself a well-known return predictor and, because the accrual base is not guaranteed zero-mean cross-sectionally, part of any result may simply be the RE/AT main effect rather than the claimed interaction.

Replacing the annual accrual level with a five-year cumulative flow is a real persistence-versus-event test rather than a restatement, and the signs are consistent, but requiring five years of recch/invch on top of an already 7%-coverage primitive risks a sparse, unstable sample, and the gross-margin term mismatches revt in the numerator with sale in the denominator.

The critique of the gen-1 difference form is correct and specific — it rewarded deteriorating margins with rising taxes payable — and the weakest-link conjunction is a materially different functional form that repairs the incoherent long leg while preserving the mechanism and coverage profile.

Internally consistent and a defensible conditioner swap on the archive's best-performing accrual primitive, but it is close to a mechanical crossing of two well-known anomalies (balance-sheet accruals × Novy-Marx gross profitability) and only modestly differentiated from AccrualPurityProfitStreak, so its incremental information is limited to distinguishing profitability level from profitability reliability.

This is a single-parameter horizon perturbation (DELTA 1→3) of an existing archive signal with everything else held identical — a diagnostic tweak rather than a new economic mechanism — and the three-year accrual is largely a slow-moving asset-growth proxy, so a positive result would be hard to attribute to reporting quality.

The financing-fragility channel is genuinely new to this archive and the short leg matches the hypothesis, but the non-negative rank multiplier forces the long leg to consist of *high* debt issuers with low accruals, which fights the well-documented negative net-debt-issuance premium and makes the net expected sign ambiguous rather than clean.

This is a rank→z-score respecification of the archive's CashAccumulationVsBookProfit with no change in mechanism, and the stated diagnosis is backwards — z-scoring winsorized ratios typically makes the Fama-MacBeth slope *more* outlier-sensitive, not more aligned with a decile spread that was driven by tails.

The expression's direction does match the stated hypothesis and the liability-side channel plus solvency conditioner is new to the archive, but the proposal implicitly bets *against* the payables component of the standard accrual anomaly (payable increases lower accruals and are conventionally return-enhancing) without acknowledging that tension, and apalch coverage is likely to be as thin as the ~7% recch/invch signals.

Replacing cross-sectional accrual scaling with a within-firm time-series position is a substantive, well-motivated design question rather than a cosmetic variant, and the clean hold-everything-else-constant construction makes the outcome interpretable — though a five-observation TS_RANK is nearly as coarse as the conditioner granularity the proposal elsewhere criticizes.

This is a mechanical ensemble of two archive signals (`AccrualPurityProfitStreak` and `FirmRelativeAccrualSurprise`) that averages two highly correlated normalizations of the *identical* accrual numerator with an unchanged conditioner, so it is a cosmetic blend rather than a new economic mechanism.

Averaging the ranks of the two conditioners already tested separately (`AccrualPurityGrossProfit` and `AccrualPurityProfitStreak`) on an otherwise unchanged expression is a signal-blending exercise whose likely outcome is an interpolation of the two prior results, and it cannot distinguish complementarity from simple diversification of noise.

The expression contradicts its own reasoning — with a non-negative RANK(NEG(Δdltt)) weight the short leg becomes high-accrual *debt reducers*, not the "accrual-building debt issuers" the hypothesis claims to short, and the long leg (low-accrual debt retirers) largely re-expresses the published net-debt-issuance anomaly.

A single, economically well-motivated change of normalization (industry-demeaning the clean accrual primitive) that cleanly isolates the confound the archive's only IND_ZSCORE signal left unresolved, though it is an incremental refinement of a known accrual construct rather than a new mechanism.

The change-in-accrual channel is genuinely untested in this archive and the sign convention matches the stated deceleration story, but note the construction NEG(Δaccrual) = accrual_{t-1} − accrual_t loads *positively* on the prior-year accrual level, which works against the Sloan effect and should be diagnosed if the result is weak.

Stacking a third hurdle onto `PayoutValidatedAccrualQuality` is mechanical corner-purity escalation whose binding third leg is the published gross-profitability anomaly, and the archive's MIN-form results (two of three with negative alphas) give little reason to expect the triple minimum to sharpen rather than dilute the cross-sectional slope.

This is a single-operator swap (ZSCORE→IND_ZSCORE) on the archive's best-performing `UnfundedAccrualBuild` that simply stacks the two strongest existing axes, so it carries high redundancy risk and its "compounding" claim cannot be distinguished from an ensemble average of two already-validated parents.

Internally consistent and economically coherent, but it is a mechanical cross of two archive winners' best pieces (liquidity deflator × tax conditioner) with no new economic content beyond what each parent already established, so the informational upside is modest even though the stated diagnostic (interpolate vs. exceed) is a fair test.

A genuinely useful identification exercise that separates the confounded scaling-versus-conditioning interpretations of the archive's strongest result, with a coherent constraint mechanism (cash relative to total liabilities) and a sign direction that matches the expression's construction.

Decomposing the accrual into its unverifiable asset leg is a well-motivated primitive-level test (and directly probes the archive's anomalous negative payable-stretch result), though the asset-side accrual decomposition is close to established soft-accrual/inventory-change work and so is more incremental than the reasoning implies.

A one-operator wrapper on an existing archive signal, but it is aimed at a specifically diagnosed FMB/alpha divergence with a plausible mechanism (industry-clustered payout regimes), which makes it a legitimate if low-ambition refinement; note that ni − Δre is essentially net distributions, so the signal is largely a payout-minus-accrual composite and may load on the dividend/payout literature.

This is an explicit symbolic reconstruction of the Jones-model discretionary-accrual residual, whose return predictability is a long-published anomaly (Xie 2001), and the normal-accrual term additionally carries a mild scaling inconsistency (actual accrual is deflated by current sales while the expected accrual is implicitly deflated by lagged sales).

A coherent, sign-consistent pairing of the archive's two strongest legs (asset-side accrual numerator, cash-to-liabilities constraint) that is not itself in the archive, though it remains an interpolation between two validated parents and `che` still enters both legs, so a modest gain over `ConstrainedFirmAccrualPricing` would be uninformative about whether the interaction adds anything.

The non-cash-current-asset ("least reliable accrual") decomposition scaled by activity and conditioned on profitability is essentially the Richardson-Sloan-Soliman-Tuna accrual-reliability result, and relative to the archive it changes only the deflator of `AssetSideUnfundedAccrual`, making it a clean ablation but a low-information one to spend a slot on.

The accrual × leverage/distress interaction is close to published accrual-distress conditioning, and `lt/ceq` is a badly behaved conditioner because negative or near-zero book equity — precisely the most fragile firms the hypothesis targets — produces negative or explosive ratios that rank at the wrong end, so a weak result would not cleanly distinguish leverage from liquidity as the hypothesis claims.

The expression does not compute the stated mechanism — `NEG(ABS(ni/sale))` weights small losses identically to the small *profits* that the benchmark-beating story is about, and it also loads on low-profitability firms generally, directly opposing the archive's validated finding that accruals are most informative among persistently profitable and high-gross-profit firms; an asymmetric small-positive-margin indicator would test the hypothesis properly.

This is a deflator rescaling of an existing archive primitive rather than a new mechanism, and `ceq` is the weakest of the available scalers because negative and near-zero book equity flips signs and generates extreme values that winsorization will crudely truncate, so the test is unlikely to resolve anything economically.

Genuinely combines two economically distinct and separately validated legs — asset-side unfunded accrual capacity and the margin-decline incentive — with a consistent sign and no shared inputs, so a joint improvement would be attributable to the interaction rather than to redundancy, with the only caveat being deflator instability when `MA(che,3)` is near zero.

Economically coherent as a double-condition weakest link, but the stated justification is factually wrong — `che` appears in both the accrual numerator (`act - che`) and the net-debt conditioner, and `sale` is both the deflator and the margin denominator — and the hard `INDICATOR` gate reimports exactly the zero mass point that this batch's own sibling proposal diagnoses as the defect flattening the FMB slope.

A well-diagnosed repair that replaces a discontinuous gate with a strictly positive weakest-link conditioner whose two legs (thin margin, unbroken profit record) are economically distinct and jointly identify the benchmark-pressure population, though the claim of continuity is overstated since the five-year profit streak is a coarse 0–5 integer that will still produce large rank ties.

Liability maturity is a genuinely orthogonal fragility dimension to the size-of-claims proxies already validated, and it deliberately avoids `che` in the conditioner, giving a clean robustness test — the main caveat being the large mass of zero-`dltt` firms that will pile up at the top rank and may make the long/short leg composition size- and industry-tilted.

A single-component swap rather than a new mechanism, but the attribution logic is sound (full-accrual/sale numerators produced positive alphas with three different conditioners while asset-side/sale numerators produced negative ones twice), so the test cleanly isolates whether the demand-deceleration channel is salvageable — just recognize the outcome is largely diagnostic, not a candidate signal in its own right.

The base term is the level of non-cash net working capital scaled by sales with a negative sign, which is effectively the working-capital component of the well-documented net operating assets anomaly (Hirshleifer et al. 2004) in its published direction, and the proposal presents it as a novel "temporal object" without acknowledging that literature; the net-indebtedness conditioner is already validated, so the incremental content is thin.

The expression correctly implements the stated "barely beat last year" gate and tests a distinct benchmark from the zero-profit threshold, but it deliberately zeroes out precisely the declining-margin firms that drove the archive's strongest incentive-channel result, so the hypothesis sits in tension with existing evidence and the hard indicator will again create a large zero mass that depresses the FMB slope.

The two conditioner legs are strongly *negatively* correlated (RANK of NEG current margin vs RANK of the 3-year average margin), so MIN does not encode "solid record but thin now" — it mechanically selects mid-margin firms and contradicts the stated hypothesis, which would require a difference (record minus current) rather than a conjunction.

The industry-relative thinness idea is economically sound and untested, but the proposal simultaneously swaps in the 3-year-average-margin leg, inheriting the same anticorrelated-MIN defect and making the result unattributable to either change.

A substantively different base (own-history working-capital *stock* rather than the annual flow) crossed with the best-performing incentive conditioner, with an explicit diagnostic motivation for separating base effects from conditioner effects.

A legitimate motive×consequence pairing whose legs are positively (not oppositely) aligned so the MIN conjunction is coherent, though it is an incremental conditioner swap within an already heavily mined family and net debt is itself correlated with thin margins, risking a redundant rather than compounding interaction.

Genuinely new conditioning dimension (capacity for discretion rather than incentive or fragility) with full coverage, but the reviewer should check that multiplying the sales-scaled accrual *change* by the sales-scaled operating-asset *level* is not simply re-weighting the accrual by its own scale, which would make it a nonlinear transform of the base signal rather than a conditioning effect.

Clean, well-motivated combination of the two independently validated improvements (industry-demeaned accrual base, thin-margin/unbroken-profit conditioner) acting on distinct components of the product, and not present in the archive.

The "motive" leg is mislabeled — RANK(NEG(ni/sale)) peaks for large *losses*, not thin-but-positive margins (the archive's better-performing versions enforced profitability via the MIN with the profit-streak indicator) — and the capacity leg shares the sales deflator with the base, so the interaction partly re-weights the accrual by its own scale rather than conditioning on independent economics.

This is a mechanical 2x2 grid fill that pairs the archive's existing stock-overhang base with the verbatim conditioner from NetIndebtedThinMarginAccrual, with the same loss-firm contamination in RANK(NEG(ni/sale)) and high correlation between the net-debt and thin-margin legs, so it is a cosmetic recombination rather than a new mechanism.

Combining the flow (current recognition aggressiveness) and own-history stock (accumulated unconverted claims) into one base before conditioning is a genuinely distinct construction rather than a deflator tweak, and the internal logic and sign are coherent, though it remains an incremental extension of a heavily mined family and SUMRANK may blur the two very different information horizons.

Swapping the conditioner's deflator from sale to cogs is close to cosmetic since the two are near-proportional for most firms, so it cannot cleanly diagnose the shared-scaling concern it is designed to address and is otherwise a strict subset of DiscretionCapacityAccrual.

Testing whether the mechanism lives in the within-firm rather than cross-sectional normalization of the accrual flow is a legitimate and unexplored axis with a coherent sign, but it is still grid-completion on an extensively mined base-times-conditioner space and the payoff is diagnostic rather than a new economic channel.

The claim of avoiding mechanical overlap is wrong in substance — multiplying an asset-side build by a *falling* operating-liability change is a multiplicative surrogate for the full working-capital accrual already tested throughout the archive — and a decline in payables is at least as consistent with a firm paying suppliers from strength or shrinking activity as with supplier monitoring, so the "external assessor" interpretation is not identified.
